name: Preemptible execution and cancellation
current: Custom scripts execute on the renderer thread. AbortSignal handles cooperative async code, but a synchronous loop cannot be interrupted.
acceptance: Run scripts in terminable workers/processes; Cancel must stop a deliberate loop within two seconds and leave the editor responsive.
implementation: Terminable native processes, shared run IDs and process-tree cancellation.

name: Real Jest, JUnit and NUnit adapters
current: Unsupported framework modes now fail visibly. There is no installed backend for these engines.
acceptance: Discover actual project tests, execute their native runners, parse machine-readable results and distinguish zero-tests, failures and runtime errors.
implementation: Actual Jest/JUnit/NUnit project discovery, native reports and zero/failure/error controls.

name: A native language runtime registry
current: Java/C# execution depends on configured remote services or limited compatibility modes, rather than a managed local JDK/.NET runtime.
acceptance: Probe installed runtimes, show versions/capabilities, execute native fixtures locally and report missing dependencies before Run.
implementation: Native runtime registry, version probes, explicit project prerequisites and editable runtime locations.

name: Durable run sessions and process-tree cancellation
current: Playwright has a bounded child timeout, but there is no shared run-session API, cancellation token or resumable process registry across engines.
acceptance: Assign run IDs; stream stdout/stderr; cancel child trees and persist terminal status after renderer reload or crash.
implementation: Durable execution records, streamed output, interrupted-run recovery and SQLite terminal evidence.

name: A debugger protocol shared by every engine
current: Breakpoint/step fixes apply to visual steps. Python, shell and generated repository tests do not expose a unified debugger session.
acceptance: Provide engine capabilities, breakpoint validation, variable inspection and reliable stop/resume with protocol-level integration tests.
implementation: Shared capability protocol; real V8 authored breakpoints, variables and stepping. Other engines explicitly report unavailable interactive debugging.

name: Reusable fixtures and parameter schemas
current: Suite parameters and unit setup code are independent, loosely typed inputs. Shared fixtures are copied rather than versioned dependencies.
acceptance: Add typed parameter validation, reusable setup/cleanup fixtures and explicit secret parameters; cleanup runs even when setup or assertions fail.
implementation: Versioned setup/cleanup fixtures, typed parameters and memory-only secret references.

name: A real headless CI execution service
current: Generated CI templates now validate terminal JSON summaries. The corresponding hosted/headless execution API is not supplied by this desktop repository.
acceptance: Ship an authenticated CLI/service returning documented total/passed/failed/errors and nonzero exit for failure, error, pending or zero tests; exercise GitHub/GitLab/Jenkins fixtures against it.
implementation: Authenticated CLI/loopback service, genuine terminal counts and provider templates invoking the shipped runner.

name: Parallel graph scheduling and resource locks
current: The DAG runs sequentially after topological sorting. The comment mentions future parallelism, but no scheduler or concurrency control exists.
acceptance: Run independent nodes concurrently with configurable limits and per-resource locks; preserve dependency isolation, cancellation and deterministic evidence.
implementation: Parallel dependency scheduler, bounded concurrency and resource locks.

name: Explicit artifact contracts and provenance
current: Ancestor filtering is repaired, but artifacts still merge by string key. Two ancestors can publish the same name without an explicit conflict strategy.
acceptance: Add typed ports, producer/run provenance and validation; reject ambiguous collisions or require an explicit mapping before execution.
implementation: Typed input/output editors, explicit mappings, collision checks and producer/run provenance.

name: Run history, retries and failure strategies
current: Pipelines store lastRun/lastStatus and an in-memory console. There is no durable per-node run graph, retry policy or resumable execution.
acceptance: Persist every attempt and node state; implement bounded backoff, stop/continue policies and safe rerun-from-failed-node with linked original evidence.
implementation: Persisted node attempts, bounded retries, failure policy and linked rerun-from-failed evidence.

name: Versioned workflow schema and graph validation
current: Saved graph objects have no formal schema/version migration layer. Cycle errors are handled at run time.
acceptance: Validate dangling edges, duplicate IDs, missing configuration and cycles before Save/Run; migrate old underscore types without data loss.
implementation: Versioned graph schema, migration and pre-save/run structural validation.

name: Portable workflow import, templates and scheduling
current: Test sharing exists; a complete portable workspace/pipeline package and background scheduler do not. Removed automatic demo suites must not return.
acceptance: Export versioned dependency bundles; offer explicitly chosen templates without seeding user data; add opt-in schedules with missed-run policy and cancellation.
implementation: Explicit templates, checksummed fixture bundles and workspace-scoped opt-in schedules; imports disable timers.

name: OS-backed credential storage and redaction
evidence: visual-editor.js: cfg-ai-apikey and node.data.apiKey; script.js: execution_config
current: API keys/configuration can be persisted with application data or graph objects. There is no central credential reference store or general log/export redactor.
acceptance: Store secrets with Electron safeStorage/OS facilities, persist opaque references, redact exports/logs and test backups for accidental secret inclusion.
implementation: OS-encrypted vault, protected legacy configs, opaque references, actual protected HTTP and redacted evidence.

name: Workspace trust and scoped desktop capabilities
current: The renderer can request filesystem and command operations. Running user-authored tests is intentional, but there is no explicit workspace trust/capability model.
acceptance: Bind each run to a selected workspace, validate IPC payloads and sender, scope read/write/command access and require explicit trust for imported executable workflows.
implementation: Validated main-frame IPC, canonical workspace scope, imported-code review and stale read/write binding.

name: Actual infrastructure scanner adapters
current: The old green stubs are replaced by explicit unavailable errors. No Docker, Kubernetes or network scanning backend ships in the app.
acceptance: Implement separately installable, versioned adapters with authorized targets, structured findings, coverage/error state and real positive/negative fixtures.
implementation: Versioned installable local configuration/network adapters, authorized targets and explicit unsupported modes.

name: Dependency resolution from lockfiles and SBOMs
current: OSV lookups now fail incomplete coverage for unresolved ranges. Exact direct versions work, but transitive lockfile inventory is absent.
acceptance: Parse package-lock/pnpm/yarn/Python lockfiles or CycloneDX; deduplicate exact versions, track every lookup and fail incomplete coverage without losing findings.
implementation: Supported lockfile/SBOM exact-version inventory, deduplication and complete lookup accounting.

name: Scanner evidence, policy scope and suppressions
current: Local checks are pattern based. There is no syntax-aware taint analysis, reviewed suppression workflow or signed coverage record.
acceptance: Document supported rules/languages, add locations and fingerprints, expiring reviewed suppressions and explicit completeness; never advertise heuristic checks as proof of security.
implementation: Stated rule coverage, locations/fingerprints, policy scope and expiring reviewed suppressions.

name: Controlled preview isolation and network policy
current: Uploaded HTML/JS runs for testing and desktop IPC can execute authored commands. Cross-origin and untrusted-content behavior needs a deliberate trust design.
acceptance: Separate preview origin/process from privileged renderer, restrict bridge exposure, define CSP/network policy and test that untrusted content cannot access desktop capabilities.
implementation: Static picker snapshots, isolated browser execution and authenticated allowlisted DOM evidence.

name: Transactional workspace persistence and backup
current: Concurrent in-process suite mutations are repaired. Suites/settings/history remain split across localStorage and IndexedDB rather than one transactional workspace store.
acceptance: Introduce schema-versioned SQLite/IndexedDB storage, transactional multi-record changes, export/import backup and recovery tests for quota, abort, corruption and interrupted migration.
implementation: SQLite/WAL transactions, durable migrations, quota/recovery controls and visual corrupt-database archive recovery.

name: Cross-window conflict detection
current: The mutation queue protects one renderer. Multiple windows/processes or cloud writers do not share that queue or revision compare-and-swap.
acceptance: Use record revisions and atomic writes; surface conflict UI, merge/reload choices and tests with two actual app windows.
implementation: Actual two-window CAS, field-selection merges, reload, draft export and deleted-record copy.

name: A complete portable project archive
current: Sharing covers suites/snapshots. Referenced datasets, environment secrets, baselines, pipelines and artifact history are not one validated portable archive.
acceptance: Define an archive manifest with checksums/schema, include selected dependencies, exclude secrets by default and validate/preview imports before atomic commit.
implementation: Checksummed selected record dependencies, binary evidence, native baselines/configuration and precommit validation.

name: Authenticated team workspaces and permissions
current: Share/export helpers and configurable storage are not a full team service with roles, audit log, conflict resolution and tenant isolation.
acceptance: Provide authenticated identities, owner/editor/viewer policies, revocable shares, server-enforced authorization and concurrent edit tests.
implementation: Authenticated loopback team service, server roles, identity revocation and concurrent revisions.

name: Artifact storage and retention controls
current: Screenshots/history use browser storage with fixed caps. There is no configurable filesystem artifact repository, quota management or retention UI.
acceptance: Store binary artifacts by run ID, show disk usage, configure retention and pin evidence; deletions must preserve pinned runs and report recoverable errors.
implementation: Binary/log/result artifacts by run, disk usage, pinning and previewable retention.

name: Dataset types, large files and privacy controls
current: CSV escaping and literal replacement are repaired. There is no typed schema, streaming import or masking/generation policy for sensitive columns.
acceptance: Validate required/type/range constraints with row-level errors, stream large inputs and offer deterministic synthetic data plus opt-in masking.
implementation: Typed/ranged/required streaming CSV validation, saved datasets, deterministic generation, masking and explicit row batches.

name: Accessible application navigation and dialogs
current: SVG icons, focus-visible styling and reduced motion are added. Full modal focus trapping, return focus, keyboard graph editing and screen-reader coverage remain incomplete.
acceptance: Audit with a keyboard and screen reader, implement dialog semantics/focus lifecycle and accessible graph alternatives; test common flows at 200% zoom.
implementation: Named accessibility tree, semantic dialogs, trapped Tab, Escape/focus return, accessible workflow list and 200% zoom.
remaining: Automated accessibility-tree, keyboard and 200% zoom controls pass; an actual screen-reader session remains unverified.

name: Capability-aware onboarding and diagnostics
current: A fresh profile starts empty. There is no unified capability page explaining which local/remote engines are ready, missing or unsupported.
acceptance: Show runtime/browser/adapter versions, test connections, actionable recovery and exportable redacted diagnostics; never use a green badge for an unavailable engine.
implementation: Guided empty start, runtime/adapter diagnostics, truthful unavailable states, recovery and redacted exports.

name: Signed releases, installer tests and update strategy
current: An unpacked Windows build can be verified locally. There is no configured publisher certificate, signed release pipeline or verified auto-update feed.
acceptance: Add reproducible release CI, signing/secrets management, install/uninstall and upgrade tests, release checksums and a signed rollback-capable update policy.
implementation: Protected signing workflow, installer lifecycle/upgrade controls, checksums and verified signed update/rollback policy.
remaining: A publisher certificate and a genuinely signed candidate are still required.

name: Portable development and CI verification
current: Regression/E2E evidence is local Windows evidence. Python engines and browser payload preparation are explicit requirements; other OS distributions are not validated.
acceptance: Run clean-clone setup in Windows CI, install pinned test extras and retain screenshots/logs; add macOS/Linux only after real platform jobs pass.
implementation: Pinned preparation, Windows CI configuration, clean-directory installation and actual source/desktop verification.
remaining: The hosted Windows workflow has no remote execution receipt; local clean-directory evidence is separate.

name: Modular architecture and stable extension API
current: The application still uses large global scripts, inline event handlers and compatibility SVG hydration for legacy dynamic views.
acceptance: Extract modules with typed contracts, remove global load-order dependencies, publish extension capabilities and migrate remaining legacy renderers to semantic SVG components.
implementation: Explicit service/compiler contracts, typed extension capabilities and dependency-validated synchronous legacy facade with direct SVG.

name: Project governance, documentation and release notes
current: The original repository had no explicit project license, support policy or release process. A README cannot choose legal licensing on the owner’s behalf.
acceptance: Owner selects a license; add contribution guidelines, compatibility/support matrix, changelog and issue templates that request reproducible redacted evidence.
implementation: Owner-selected MIT, contribution/security/support guidance, issue template and versioned release notes.
